articles.headline: Neville's Man Utd warning: 'Get a grip or face worrying few weeks'
keyFacts: Manchester United drew 1-1 with 10-man Tottenham on Saturday, extending their winless run to four games in all competitions.
Pundit Gary Neville warned that United players must get a grip or face a worrying few weeks following their poor start to the season.
Michael Carrick's side will next play an away match against Atletico Madrid in the Champions League on Tuesday.
body: Gary Neville warns Man Utd players to 'get a grip' or face a 'worrying few weeks' after draw with 10-man Spurs

Man Utd were held to a 1-1 draw by 10-man Spurs, leaving them with one win from six Premier League games; Michael Carrick's side are away to Atletico Madrid and Leeds next; Gary Neville: "If you're not quite right there from a mental and physical perspective, you're going to get found out"
Saturday 10 October 2026 21:00, UK
Gary Neville warned that Manchester United could be in for a "worrying few weeks" if their players don't "get a grip" on their season.
Michael Carrick's side's poor start to the campaign continued as Dominic Solanke's late goal rescued a draw for 10-man Spurs at Old Trafford on Saturday.
There were boos from the home fans, both at half-time and full-time, as United extended their winless run to four games in all competitions, keeping them 12th in the Premier League.

They now face a daunting run of fixtures, starting with a Champions League away game against Atletico Madrid on Tuesday before Sunday's Premier League trip to Elland Road to face Leeds, live on Sky Sports.

Speaking on The Gary Neville Podcast, Neville questioned the midfield pairing of Youri Tielemans and Kobbie Mainoo and said the side's plight could worsen if their players don't show improvement.
"Tielemans and Mainoo, I think we've seen enough of it now," Neville said.
"I'm not calling time on it because that's probably too drastic but I've seen enough to think that's not a midfield that's dynamic enough to play at this football club in the Premier League.
"I think they are both good players, by the way, individually. But sometimes you just have players that don't quite knit together or don't quite suit each other.
"I think when [Carlos] Baleba came on with Mainoo, it looked like there was a lot more energy.
"There's going to have to be something done in there, and the rest of them are going to have to get a grip because they are going to a Diego Simeone Atletico Madrid and Elland Road.
"If you're not quite right there from a mental and physical perspective, you're going to get found out.
"They've got a couple of days to recover, pick themselves up from this, and get going because if they don't get going, it's going to be a worrying few weeks."
The draw with Spurs was the third game this season in which Manchester United have failed to win when leading, following the 2-2 draw with Everton and the 3-2 loss to Brighton in the Carabao Cup.
Jamie Redknapp felt their performance showed a lack of cohesion as well as a lack of resilience.
"Brighton in the Carabao Cup, they were 2-0 up and lost 3-2," he said on Sky Sports. "That is unprecedented and does not happen at Old Trafford, except it does with this team.
"I don't see enough connections in that midfield and they look devoid of any confidence, ideas, or patterns of play, playing out the back.
"Tottenham were just much better than them in every department, but that is just a theme this season.
"Their energy levels are not good enough and they look loose going forward. There was no real structure.
"The squad is not good or strong enough and Michael [Carrick] needs help in that respect."

articles.headline: Jailbroken PS5s Can Now Emulate PS2 Games Using Physical Discs
keyFacts: Lead coder Swordpdf announced that the new PS5SX2 emulator allows jailbroken PlayStation 5 consoles to play physical PlayStation 2 discs by dumping them to the SSD.
Hardware limitations prevent the PS5 from reading CD-based PlayStation 2 discs and PlayStation 1 discs because the console's optical drive cannot read CDs.
Swordpdf announced that a PS3 disc emulator called PS5SX3 is currently in development.
body: The vibe-coded horror show continues to get worse for Sony, as thereâs now a new, Claude-coded version of the PCSX2 emulator, named PS5SX2, that can be installed on jailbroken PlayStation 5s and allows users to dump their PlayStation 2 games to the consoleâs SSD to emulate them. Unfortunate timing for Sony, considering the most recent PS5 jailbreaking advancements.

Of course, using a PS5 to emulate PS2 games isnât technically new, so why is this headline-worthy? Because the latest version of PS5SX2 allows you to emulate games using your PS2 discs. No need to download a ROM from a sketchy website anymore; you just pop your own PS2 disc in your PS5 disc tray and dump it directly from there.

This news comes directly from Swordpdf, PS5SX2âs lead coder. As they detailed in a post on X, and in PS5SX2âs GitHub README, PS5SX2 version 2.01 can indeed read and dump physical PS2 discs. As Swordpdf explains in the PS5SX2 version 2.01 release update on GitHub, once you âput a PS2 disc in the drive,â PS5SX2 then âdumps it if not already dumped and launches the game.â
PS2 discs. Straight into a PS5.
20+ years of nostalgia, one disc away.

However, there is a catch: due to a specific hardware limitation, it appears that a PS5 running PS5SX2 canât be used with all PlayStation 2 discs and, by extension, any PlayStation 1 discs.

The PlayStation 5âs disc drive can read Blu-Rays and DVDs, but it cannot read CDs. That means that any of the blue-tinted PlayStation 2 discs (which are CDs, not DVDs) canât be read by the PS5âs optical drive laser, and therefore canât be burned to the SSD or an external HDD using PS5SX2. Likewise, PS1 discs are CDs, so the same issue applies there.

And yes, before you ask, PS5SX2 is an AI-assisted project. No need to guess or investigate on that front, as Swordpdf is quite upfront about this. Plus, Claude is literally one of the three contributors listed on PS5SX2âs GitHub.

But Swordpdf isnât quite finished ruining Sonyâs week just yet, as theyâve already announced that a PS5SX3 emulator, which will allow PS3 games to be dumped on the PS5 from a disc, is in the works on both X and in their Discord server. Swordpdf also seems to think they can do the same for PS1 discs, but considering that shouldnât physically be possible, I donât know how thatâs going to pan out.

articles.headline: It took Squadron 42 14 years but it finally crawled onto Steam
keyFacts: Fourteen years after its initial announcement, Squadron 42 now has an official Steam page where users can add it to their wishlists.
Cloud Imperium aims to launch the game within the second quarter of 2027 following another delay from its intended release window.
Squadron 42 is a more focused project than Star Citizen, featuring A-list actors, top-notch graphics, and high-end mechanics.
body: Fourteen years after its initial announcement, Squadron 42 is finally on Steam and available for wishlisting. While the game still doesn’t have a specific release date, it aims to launch sometime within the second quarter of 2027 after getting delayed (again).

Squadron 42 , Star Citizen ‘s more focused and more apparent little brother, seems to be reaching the end of its development after 14 very long years in production. The game now has an official Steam page, which you can visit to wishlist the game in anticipation of its Q2 2027 release date. While the game was supposed to release this year, it was delayed once again into the next, though if the Steam page is anything to go by, Cloud Imperium might actually stick to this latest plan after all.
Image via Roberts Space Industries Read what’s behind the latest news in gaming (with a bit of snark) by subscribing to the Destructoid Checkpoint newsletter !

However, since Squadron 42 was meant to come out in 2014, i.e., 12 years ago, delays can always happen. Both it and Star Citizen have been in somewhat of a production stasis where they are constantly and simultaneously around the corner and years away, despite hundreds of millions of dollars poured into the projects via crowdfunding. In fact, Star Citizen has received over a billion in funding since it first began its journey through (but not to) the stars, and yet it still remains the most elusive game out there.

We’ve written time and again about how many players out there consider these games to be a borderline scam, considering the amount of money poured in and what has been delivered. But to play devil’s advocate here, Star Citizen really has delivered a lot so far, and the innovations it’s trying to achieve are nothing short of fascinating, and if it ever does come out in full, it’ll be the most advanced online game to date.

But that’s the crux of the issue with CIE and its project: the dream is as much the product as the game itself. The idea of achieving, of getting to that point, the infinite journey toward the center of the universe.

Thankfully, Squadron 42 has always been a more focused project and much smaller in scope, though it does have all the makings of a AAA behemoth. A-list actors, top-notch graphics and mechanics, the whole shebang. So, perhaps Q2 will start us toward seeing Star Citizen completed, too. Who knows.

articles.headline: Apple discloses deal to hire team and license tech from personalized podcast startup Huxe
keyFacts: Apple disclosed in a regulatory filing with the European Commission that it reached a reverse acqui-hire deal with personalized audio startup Huxe.
The agreement allows Apple to make employment offers to certain Huxe employees and receive a non-exclusive license to the startup's intellectual property.
The regulatory filing does not state which individuals received job offers, whether they accepted, or what Apple plans to do with the technology.
body: Apple revealed in a regulatory filing that it has reached an agreement to bring on team members and technology from personalized audio startup Huxe, in what’s commonly known as a reverse acqui-hire deal.

As first reported in MacRumors, Apple disclosed to the European Commission that it has agreed to make employment offers to “certain employees of Huxe AI,” and to “receive a non-exclusive license to Huxe’s intellectual property rights.”

Reverse acqui-hires emerged in recent years as a way for larger companies to hire key team members and license technology from startups without acquiring the startups outright — presumably allowing them to build up AI talent and tech without drawing as much antitrust scrutiny. (Confusingly, these deals have both been referred to as “reverse acqui-hires” and as plain old “acqui-hires.”)

In the case of Huxe, the startup was founded by developers who’d previously worked on the AI-generated podcast features in NotebookLM (recently renamed Gemini Notebook). But Huxe announced on May 21 that it was shutting down, with the team posting on the Huxe website that the company would be removing its app from the Apple and Google stores, halting service, and deleting user data.

“The team is moving on to new things, and we won’t be continuing development of the product,” the company said. It also thanked its users, saying, “The fact that you used it, told friends about it, sent us your suggestions and your ideas, made it feel like we built it together.”
On June 9, shortly after Huxe’s announcement, Apple notified the European Commission of its deal.
The filing does not say who received employment offers or if they accepted. Nor does it disclose anything about Apple’s plans.

Possibly related: Huxe’s shutdown announcement came just a day after Spotify unveiled AI-powered podcast generation features of its own, so Apple could be hoping to add similar functionality to its Podcasts app. Tech executives seem enamored with the idea that personalized audio can replace regular podcasts (and maybe even parent-child interaction?), though it’s not clear how many normal listeners agree.

articles.headline: GTA 6 leaker CyberLeek is now reportedly threatening to release a full, playable build of the game
keyFacts: A GTA 6 leaker named CyberLeek threatened to release a full, playable build of the game if a cryptocurrency coin reaches a market cap of $30 million.

body: A GTA 6 leaker has reportedly threatened to put out a complete, playable build of the game, start to finish.
The threat was posted on CyberLeek's website after the leaker shared 25 minutes of footage from the game earlier this week.

Rockstar has previously issued statements regarding the leaker, noting that the leaks are "heartbreaking" and that "this is obviously not how we intended for you to see the game after all this time". Take-Two, Rockstar's parent company, has been hunting for the person behind the leaks, and has tried to subpoena Discord for information pertaining to the leaker's identity.

After going quiet for a bit, CyberLeek came back with a bang this week, posting new footage from Rockstar's upcoming game that even features nude scenes, including a fully naked Jason, and a topless Lucia. Eurogamer has seen the video, and it appears to be legitimate - and, as is now traditional, has CyberLeek's emblem overlaid on top of the footage.
CyberLeek now reportedly says the build will go out if their cryptocurrency coin reaches a market cap of $30 million, and claims it can be played through to the end credits.

"Here's the deal, nice and clean," the demand reads. "CyberLeek hits 30 million marketcap, the build goes out — full story mode, played to the end, credits and all. Don't believe it has full story mode? Ask for what you want to see, and it gets provided. Take-Two gets one way out: physical disks and a public apology. They can take it at any moment. Or they can gamble that CL is bluffing. Everyone knows which one they'll pick."
GTA 6 is due out on PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X/S on 19th November.

articles.headline: The communist despots who rejected the label —until they gained power
keyFacts: The New York Post reported that past leaders like Fidel Castro, Hugo Chavez, and Daniel Ortega rejected communist labels before securing power.
Those leaders initially claimed their movements were humanistic or mixed before their regimes seized property and established socialist or communist rule.
Michigan Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed insisted he is a capitalist and not a socialist, his campaign told The Post.
body: A long line of future communist despots rejected the socialist and communist label — until they secured power.
As politicians, revolutionaries, and military officers, they knew better than to blurt out an affiliation that might cause them headaches abroad that could impact their performance at home.

Among the members of the notorious list was Cuba’s Fidel Castro, who famously visited New York City, complete with a stop at Yankee Stadium, after leading the revolution that drove the Batista regime from power in 1959.

Castro proclaimed that “our revolution is a humanistic one” and that “I have said very clearly that we are not Communists.” He went on to establish a communist regime with an iron grip on power that has held for 67 years and counting.

Venezuelan dictator Hugo Chavez, a former Army officer, followed the lead of his mentor Castro with the “humanist” label before declaring a socialist revolution and crusading against the US. The US now holds his successor Nicolas Maduro, who is facing narco-terrorism charges, after seizing him in a January raid.

Infamous Cambodian dictator Pol Pot formed the communist party of Kampuchia in secret, instead rallying around anti-imperialist principles and deploying the opaque phrase Angkar or “the organization.”
Soon after defeating a US-backed government in 1975, his totalitarian regime abolished private property and turned to forced deportations to the labor camps in the countryside.

Sandinista Daniel Ortega in Nicaragua took power from the Somoza regime and later proclaimed that “political pluralism and a mixed economy” were central to the revolution. His Marxist-Leninist followed by seizing large agricultural enterprises and corporations.

While even his staunchest critics haven’t compared him to a despot, Michigan Democratic Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed — who has ties to top radicals in the Democratic Socialists of America — insisted this week he is a “capitalist” and his campaign told The Post he has said he is “not a socialist” and “has never been a member of the DSA.”

articles.headline: 'Time for Ukraine to get new president,' says Trump after Zelensky condemns diesel deal
keyFacts: US President Donald Trump said Ukraine needs a new leader after Volodymyr Zelensky criticized a deal suspending sanctions on Russian diesel exports.
Zelensky warned the deal funds Russia's war, while Trump argued Ukrainian strikes on refineries worsen global fuel shortages.
EU foreign affairs chief Kaja Kallas said European ministers plan to approve their largest sanctions package against Russia on Monday.
body: - Published
US President Donald Trump has said he thinks "it's time for Ukraine to get a new president" as he responded to Volodymyr Zelensky's criticism of the US diesel deal with Russia.

The Ukrainian president warned a new deal to release millions of tonnes of Russian diesel into the US would provide Moscow with money to continue its war against his nation, calling it a gift to Russian President Vladimir Putin.
Trump told reporters outside the White House on Saturday that Zelensky "wants to make problems for the world" by continuing to authorise attacks on Russian refineries.
"He'd better damn well stop," Trump said, before suggesting Ukraine should "get a new leader who can make a deal".

Global fuel supplies, including diesel, have been severely limited by the war against Iran launched by the US and Israel, which led to the effective closure of the Strait of Hormuz, through which roughly a fifth of the world's oil products usually flows.
Russia - a major producer - and Ukraine have recently intensified their strikes on each other's energy infrastructure and transport facilities, further straining energy markets.
"We said, 'you can do whatever you want to Russia, don't hit the refineries', because that's a world problem that's caused," Trump continued.
"He could have made many deals and for some reason, he never does."
Putin's envoy Kirill Dmitriev described Trump's intervention as "iconic and historic", saying that Ukraine "needs leadership actually focused on peace".
The US president confirmed on Friday that an agreement had been reached with Moscow to suspend sanctions on Russian diesel exports until 7 April.
Zelensky reacted by saying it would allow Moscow to raise new funds to source new military equipment to continue the war.
He also accused Moscow of taking the deal "to mean they can keep fighting, to mean they keep dropping bombs on cities" following deadly new strikes on Zaporizhzhia.
The Ukrainian president spoke to several allies on Saturday to discuss the latest developments, calling for "real decisions to protect lives in Ukraine" and to protect European security.
A Downing Street spokesperson said UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham had spoken to Zelensky and offered his "complete solidarity".

The pair had agreed Russia should acquiesce to "an immediate energy ceasefire" and end its attacks on shipping in the Black Sea, the spokesperson said, as "this would immediately release more energy and food supplies into the global market".

News of the US-Russia diesel deal was also met with criticism by EU's foreign affairs chief Kaja Kallas, who echoed Zelensky in saying that suspending sanctions "provides Moscow with more revenues to wage war", adding: "This is not the time to ease pressure on Russia, and Europe won't."
She said European foreign ministers intended to approve the biggest set of sanctions on Russia since the start of its full-scale invasion on Monday.
The deal with Russia is the latest effort from Trump to lower fuel prices in the US ahead of the midterm elections, after months spent grappling with the political consequences of the Iran war.

That conflict, which began in February, has sent the cost of petrol and in particular diesel skyrocketing, which has soured his standing with the American public who have been stung by the higher pump prices and knock-on effects that led to across-the-board inflation.
The average price of diesel is currently $6.28 (Â£4.74) a gallon, according to the AAA â up from last month's $5.94 average, and $3.68 last year.
Under the deal, Russia would release an initial 300,000 tonnes of diesel "to the American and global marketplace" followed by an additional 500,000 tonnes in November.

A further million would follow, Trump wrote on Truth Social, and then another 3m tonnes "within a short period of time" â but he noted that this delivery will be "based on the condition of their diesel refineries".
In the past 10 months, Russia experienced two waves of severe fuel shortages across the country due to Ukrainian drones strikes on its oil refineries.
Diesel production in Russia dropped by an estimated 30%, according to the International Energy Agency.
Trump had already called for new elections in Ukraine last December, external, saying Ukrainian voters should have the choice to replace Zelensky.
Since the war broke out in 2022 Ukraine has been under martial law, meaning elections are suspended.

articles.headline: Oregon vs. UCLA prediction, pick, odds, spread: Bruins looking for signature win against shorthanded Ducks
keyFacts: No. 13 Oregon and No. 21 UCLA will play Saturday in a game with major College Football Playoff implications.
Oregon quarterback Dante Moore is unlikely to play due to a concussion, meaning Dylan Raiola is expected to start.
CBS Sports predicts that Oregon will win the game and cover the 11.5-point spread.
body: No. 13 Oregon and No. 21 UCLA are squaring off Saturday at in game that will reverberate in the Big Ten and beyond. The 3-1 Ducks are already dealing with a thin margin for error as they prepare to host a 4-0 UCLA team that profiles as a potential dark-horse contender under first-year coach Bob Chesney.

Both are coming off bye weeks following Week 4 wins, each impressive for different reasons. Oregon took down USC 41-27 on the road and showed an explosive offensive gear, even after losing starting quarterback Dante Moore to a scary injury in the first half.

UCLA turned heads by traveling cross-country for a 54-3 win over Maryland, marked by an all-systems dominance which suggested the Bruins are no joke. While Chesney's first season since arriving from James Madison is off to a perfect start, this marks a new kind of challenge.

The Bruins have not played a team currently ranked in the top 60 of the CBS Sports 138 and will be up against Oregon, which entered the season at No. 2 in the AP poll. After a stunning Week 2 loss at Oklahoma State, the Ducks began living up to preseason expectations in their Week 4 win over the Trojans.
Where to watch Oregon vs. UCLA live
Date: Saturday, Oct. 10 | Time: 3:30 p.m. ET
Location: Autzen Stadium -- Eugene, Oregon
TV: CBS | Live stream: CBSSports.com, CBS Sports App
Streaming on Paramount+ Premium
Oregon vs. UCLA: Need to know

Dante Moore unlikely to play: Oregon quarterback Dante Moore returned to practice this week after suffering a concussion on a late hit in the first half of the Ducks' Week 4 win at USC. However, he's unlikely to play against UCLA. That should mean another opportunity for Dylan Raiola. The Nebraska transfer completed 19 of 25 passes for 289 yards and two touchdowns against USC and looked comfortable leading a talented Ducks offense. Having such a solid second option should reduce any urgency Oregon might feel to get Moore back on the field. Raiola is a former two-year starter for the Cornhuskers and a five-star prospect who is one of the nation's most talented second-string quarterbacks.

UCLA's rushing attack: UCLA ranks No. 4 nationally in rushing offense at 281.5 yards per game on the ground. James Madison transfer Wayne Knight is the name to know. The 5-foot-7 speedster is tied for third nationally with nine rushing touchdowns. He reached the 100-yard mark in each of the Bruins' first two Big Ten games. Oregon is familiar with his game after he ran for 110 yards on 17 carries in the Ducks' 51-34 victory over James Madison in last year's College Football Playoff quarterfinal. The difference this time is that Knight has a better supporting cast around him.

CFP implications: Oregon's Week 2 loss at Oklahoma State put the Ducks' postseason aspirations in early jeopardy. After UCLA, the only ranked opponent left on Oregon's schedule is Ohio State (Nov. 7). While having a manageable slate is helpful in some respects, there's also no guarantee the Ducks would make the CFP as an at-large team with two losses if there wasn't much meat on their resume. CBS Sports' College Football Forecaster projects Oregon with a 51.1% chance to make the 12-team field with a win over UCLA. That drops to 19.6% with a loss. UCLA would have a 33.3% chance to reach the CFP if it beats Oregon and an 8.3% chance with a loss.
Oregon vs. UCLA prediction, picks

UCLA's bread and butter is the run. But all four of the Bruins' wins are against teams ranked No. 65 or worse in the CBS Sports 138, and three of those four teams rank outside the top 100 in run defense. Oregon is 38th. articles.headline: Money, networks and bias: Why women struggle to win seats in US politics
keyFacts: Women hold a record high 28.4 percent of US Congress seats and 14 governorships, despite making up 51 percent of the population.
Researcher Kelly Dittmar said structural barriers, high campaign costs, male-dominated donor networks, and cultural biases make winning office harder for women.
Upcoming elections will decide congressional seats and 36 governorships, with potential historic wins for Native American and Black female candidates.
body: Around 51% of the population of the United States is female, but that is not reflected in the make-up of the US Congress, where only 28.4% of the members are women. Nevertheless, with 152 women in total sitting in the House of Representatives and Senate, the number is higher than it has ever been in the history of the United States. The number of female governors of the 50 US states is also currently higher than ever before: Some 14 of them — 28% — are women.

There are a number of reasons why there are still comparatively few female representatives in the US Congress. "Some of them are structural: There are rules and processes in place in our political system that make it harder for any newcomers to break in," says Kelly Dittmar, director of research at the Center for American Women and Politics (CAWP) at Rutgers University. "Historically, women were newcomers."

Seats in the Senate only come up for election every six years. Members of the House of Representatives serve two-year terms, but there is no limit to the number of times they can stand for reelection, so in theory they can stay in office for decades.

Also, as Dittmar points out, election campaigns in the US are very expensive. Women have historically been less able to access networks of rich donors — who, like many party leaders, are still most likely to be men. Leading male politicians are also more likely to recruit men to stand as new candidates. Finally, cultural biases also play a role: "Stereotypes and expectations about what women can and should do."

The elections on November 3 will decide whether more or fewer women will sit in the US Congress over the next two years. All 435 seats in the House of Representatives and 35 of the 100 seats in the Senate are up for election in the midterms. And in 36 states, the citizens will also decide who will move in to the governor's villa.
House of Representatives: Female Democrats outnumber female Republicans three to one

125 of the 435 representatives in the House are women. As in the Senate, and also with the gubernatorial posts, they are not evenly distributed between the two parties: There are more women among the Democrats than among the Republicans. At present, there are 95 women sitting as representatives for the Democrats, and 30 for the Republicans.

"There is a far less robust support infrastructure for women within the Republican Party," says Dittmar. She comments that organizations that specifically recruit, train, and fund women candidates are almost all either on the Democrat side, or non-partisan. Besides, she adds, "A lot of the [Republican] party leaders don't see an electoral incentive or pressure" to recruit more women. Diversity is more important to Democrat voters, who place greater value on seeing women among their elected representatives.

The Republicans currently have a majority in the House of Representatives, which means that they also get to appoint the Speaker or majority leader. At the moment, the position is held by Mike Johnson. Only one woman has held this powerful post to date: Nancy Pelosi, who was the Democrats' Speaker from 2007 to 2011, and again from 2019 to 2023.
US Senate: Even higher bar for women

Women currently constitute 27% of the US Senate – 16 Democrats and 11 Republicans. Each of the 50 states is represented by two senators. The term of office is longer in this chamber of the US Congress, and the majority of the officials here represent many more voters than the representatives in the lower house.

According to Dittmar, it's even harder for women to win a seat in the Senate. "With the Senate, it's an opportunity and timing issue," she says. Each seat comes up for election every six years. There are 100 in total, and every two years only a third of them are available. Little opportunity, then, for women who have not previously sat in the Senate to advance. A state-wide senatorial election campaign is also more expensive than the equivalent campaign for a seat in the House of Representatives — and studies indicate that female candidates are generally less wealthy than their male counterparts.

For one senatorial candidate, the November midterms could prove historic. If the Democrat Peggy Flanagan wins in Minnesota, she will be the first Native American woman to sit in the US Senate. Flanagan is Ojibwe, otherwise known as Chippewa, an indigenous people from the Great Lakes region spanning the US and Canada.

Flanagan currently holds the post of lieutenant governor of Minnesota. Polls suggest that her chances are good. She has a slight lead over her rival, the Republican Michele Tafoya, previously a sports reporter and advisor to conservative politicians.
First black woman state governor?

Ten of the current 14 female governors are Democrats, while four are Republicans. Six of the 14 are standing again, including Sarah Huckabee Sanders, the governor of Arkansas, who was President Trump's press secretary during his first term in office.

For the first time in US history, it is possible that a Black woman may be elected state governor. In Minnesota, the Democrat Tim Walz — Kamala Harris's vice-presidential candidate in the 2024 election — is not standing for reelection. The main rivals for his seat are the Democrat Amy Klobuchar and the (Black) Republican Lisa DeMuth. Meanwhile, the Black Democrat Keisha Lance Bottoms is running for governor of the state of Georgia.

Kelly Dittmar doesn't think DeMuth will win in Minnesota — the state is regarded as solidly Democrat. And Klobuchar is well known among the people there; she has represented Minnesota in the US Senate since 2007.

But in Georgia, according to Dittmar, it's a different story: "That race is considered a toss-up, 50-50." Dittmar believes that Bottoms "absolutely has a chance to be the first Black woman governor." Former President Barack Obama is her most prominent supporter, while President Trump has declared his support for the Republican candidate, Rick Jackson.
This article has been translated from German.

articles.headline: Michael Carrick warned he’s ‘in trouble’ as Manchester United sink to 40-year low against 10-man Spurs
keyFacts: Pundit Jason Cundy stated that manager Michael Carrick is in trouble after Manchester United drew with 10-man Tottenham Hotspur.
Tottenham equalised through Dominic Solanke in stoppage time after Rodrigo Bentancur received a red card for headbutting Luke Shaw.
Manchester United recorded six points from six matches, marking their lowest points tally at this stage of a league season in 40 years.
body: Michael Carrick’s job is in jeopardy following Manchester United’s draw with 10-man Tottenham Hotspur.
That is according to talkSPORT’s Jason Cundy as the Red Devils’ winless run extended to four matches.
Carrick’s side are now winless in four matches as their woes continue Getty
United were unable to see off Spurs at Old Trafford despite taking the lead with less than 20 minutes remaining.
Bryan Mbeumo’s goal was followed by a red card for Rodrigo Bentancur just five minutes later.
The Tottenham midfielder was dismissed by referee Stuart Attwell for headbutting Luke Shaw , prompting a touchline melee between players from both sides.
However, the red card was not enough to discourage Spurs, who equalised through Dominic Solanke in stoppage time.
Is Carrick under pressure?
The result lifts Roberto De Zerbi’s side off the foot of the table, although they are still without a Premier League win this season.
It could prove to be a result which is more damning for Carrick and United, though, with Cundy fearing for his future as manager.
Reacting to the final whistle on the GameDay Phone-In, he admitted: “Carrick is on the rack. I’m telling you now, he is in trouble.
“That is terrible. The last three games, they lost to 10-man Man City, could’ve got beaten by Fulham and they draw at home, 1-0 up, to 10-man Spurs.”
He continued: “They have been absolutely terrible. The heat on Carrick now is going to be unbelievable.”

Cundy’s verdict comes days after talkSPORT host Gabby Agbonlahor echoed a similar sentiment, who also claimed the likes of Antonio Conte and Eddie Howe could be waiting in the wings should a change be made.
United have made their worst start to a league season for 40 years Getty
Carrick has only been in permanent charge since May, having been rewarded with a two-year deal following his impressive spell as caretaker boss.
United make unwanted history
The stats from United’s latest draw make for unpleasant reading, with Mbeumo’s goal only their second shot on target of the match.
Meanwhile, their recent form against sides with a man less is also cause for concern.
The Red Devils have now failed to win any of their last three league matches against sides that have received a red card.
Prior to tonight, the two previous instances had ended in defeat.
Perhaps most worrying for supporters, though, is their points tally of just six points from six matches this term.
The Red Devils’ form makes for grim reading
It marks their lowest return at this stage of a league campaign since collecting four points at the start of the 1986/87 season.
Saturday’s draw follows another 1-1 stalemate away to Fulham in their previous outing.
That setback came after United had been beaten by Manchester City and Brighton in the Premier League and Carabao Cup, respectively.
As a result, Carrick’s side have not tasted victory since beating Sabah in the Champions League on September 10, exactly a month ago.
Whilst they remain 12th in the table, three of the clubs below them are still yet to play this weekend.
United themselves return to action with a trip to Atletico Madrid on Tuesday before facing Leeds United at Elland Road next weekend.

articles.headline: DSA could cause ‘civil war’ within House of Representatives: Joe Concha
keyFacts: Washington Examiner columnist Joe Concha warned that rising socialist members could threaten House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries' leadership position.
House Speaker Mike Johnson stated that Jeffries will struggle to control incoming members who want to abolish major institutions.
Concha said friction between establishment Democrats and socialist members could cause a civil war within the House.
body: Washington Examiner columnist Joe Concha said House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries (D-NY) has a tough battle to fight against rising socialist members of the Democratic Party , which could threaten his position.
Concha reacted to a clip of House Speaker Mike Johnson on Wednesday, who had advice for Jeffries.

“Hakeem is going to have a real time on his hands because there are some people who are coming in who, I believe, have ill designs for the institution. They’ve said they’d like to abolish a lot of those institutions, and it’s going to be very difficult for him to corral those folks,” Johnson told Fox News.
Concha said if the Democratic Socialists of America win elections in any “meaningful way,” Jeffries might not become the House speaker.
“They may say, ‘This guy isn’t far left enough for us, we want our own person,’” Concha said on Fox Business’s Varney & Co . Thursday.
Concha listed items from the DSA’s platform, arguing that “moderate Democrats probably don’t want to be attached to that.”
The DSA’s new platform was released on July 14.

The platform, “Workers Deserve More,” includes eliminating the U.S. Senate , granting amnesty for all immigrants , defunding the Department of War , and replacing the Electoral College with a national popular vote for president. The DSA is also calling for universal healthcare .

“Dealing with the DSA means dealing with things that are completely detached from reality, especially when you’re talking about things like government-run healthcare, which could go to the tune of trillions, which we do not have the money to pay for. But that’s what they’re talking about, and that’s what they’re campaigning on,” Concha said.
“It’s almost like two different parties at this point,” he continued.
WHO WILL SURVIVE? THE HIGH 2026 STAKES FOR TOP LEADERS IN CONGRESS

Concha said someone like Rep. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez (D-NY) would be ideal for the DSA to replace Jeffries. He said the friction between establishment Democrats and this new wave of socialists could cause an uproar.
“There could be a civil war within the lower chamber,” Concha said.

articles.headline: Two weeks with the new ModRetro Chromatic Transparent: I'm loving this slick modern way to play classic Game Boy games
keyFacts: TechRadar reviewed the ModRetro Chromatic Transparent, a handheld device that plays original Game Boy and Game Boy Color cartridges.
The new transparent version costs $149.99 / £139.99, which is $50 / £45 cheaper than the original version, and includes Tetris.
The device features a see-through plastic shell and an upgraded IPS backlit LCD screen with Gorilla Glass.
body: Over the years of multiple house moves and life events, I've somehow managed to keep hold of my original Legend of Zelda: Link's Awakening DX cartridge on Game Boy. My actual Game Boy handhelds and various other Pokémon games have all, disappointingly, been lost to time — but that one cart has stuck around. For the last two weeks, I've finally had something to play it on.

I'm talking about the latest ModRetro Chromatic Transparent: an updated version of its homage to the original Game Boy that's capable of playing all original Game Boy and Game Boy Color game cartridges, as well as ModRetro's own re-releases.

What's even more interesting is that this new version of the Chromatic doesn't just come in several transparent colorways, but also sports a much lower starting price of $149.99 / £139.99 — that's $50 / £45 cheaper than the original version. Plus, a copy of Tetris is still included with all purchases.

I've been bouncing between that classic block-based puzzler and probably one of my favorite Zelda adventures over the last couple of weeks to test out the Chromatic — and I'm super-impressed with the swish little handheld.
As much as I love the idea of playing retro games on original hardware, there's no denying the impact of some of the huge improvements the Chromatic makes over the classic Game Boy.
The design is one thing, which is made up of a see-through plastic shell that weighs just 6.2 oz (176g), making it slightly lighter and more comfortable for longer gaming sessions.

But the real highlight is the screen. It maintains the same dimensions and resolution as the original Game Boy, but upgrades it to an IPS backlit LCD with scratch-resistant Gorilla Glass. That means you get a sharp and clear image in all conditions, so long gone are the days of waiting for the next streetlight to pass to see the screen on nighttime journeys.

Maybe, though, like the Chromatic M64 before it, this will inspire me to start building another collection of retro games.

articles.headline: 10 Stephen King Movie Adaptations That Are Better Than The Books
keyFacts: Polygon published a list of 10 Stephen King movie adaptations that are considered better than their source books.
The article highlights films like The Mist, The Shining, and Misery, noting how directors used different endings, pacing, or character changes to improve upon King's writing.
According to the article, changes such as streamlining plots or adding atmospheric tension allowed these films to outshine their original novels.
body: The most successful Stephen King adaptations aren’t necessarily the most faithful. King’s name has become a brand in itself, promising versatility across more than 60 books and nearly 200 short stories. His writing is engaging and accessible, lending itself to excellent genre stories that shine on the big screen. But with such an abundant body of work, the quality of the resulting adaptations varies wildly.

In some cases, like The Lawnmower Man (1992), the adaptation has little to no connection to King’s original story — and isn’t well-made, either. Then there’s Andy Muschietti’s It movies, which have plenty of merits and even make some improvements, despite their flaws. By streamlining King’s stories, expanding certain characters, or making audacious departures from the books, they improve upon his work in unexpected ways. Here are 10 Stephen King movies that are better than the books they adapted.
1 The Mist (2007)

Endings can make or break a story, especially one as tight-paced and devastating as The Mist. Frank Darabont’s film opts for a depressing ending that even King didn’t anticipate — the author actually prefers the film’s ending to his own novella. By squashing all hope for protagonist David Drayton, The Mist becomes a cautionary tale about mob mentality and the dangers of giving up on hope. Even before arriving at such a bleak conclusion, Darabont ditches the source material’s slow-burn approach to opt for a narrative that feels like a relentless survival horror. The claustrophobia of being trapped inside a local supermarket is captured brilliantly, along with the evils of religious fanaticism, which can be more terrifying than eldritch beasts on occasion.
2 Stand By Me (1986)

King’s 1982 novella, The Body, is the basis for Rob Reiner’s heartbreaking adaptation, Stand By Me. Although The Body is spectacular in its portrayal of grief and childhood nostalgia, Stand By Me streamlines a meandering coming-of-age tale, giving it more hard-hitting focus. Reiner cuts down most of the bleakness from the novella in favor of a more grounded examination of childhood, allowing certain characters to get closure and take slightly different routes. The core cast of child actors, including a talented River Phoenix, deliver sincere performances, allowing the film to capture the fleeting friendships that define growing up, but never surface again.
3 Doctor Sleep (2019)

Mike Flanagan has proven his knack for tackling King’s source material with Doctor Sleep, a follow-up to The Shining that revolves around an adult Danny Torrance (Ewan McGregor) and revisits the horrors of the Overlook Hotel. King had famously disliked Stanley Kubrick’s rendition of The Shining, and Flanagan does his due diligence by paying tribute to both interpretations of the story. His Doctor Sleep also respects the underlying impulses of the source material, even though Flanagan improves upon it with a tighter pacing and a more satisfying climax. This is one of the rare instances where an antagonist feels more threatening onscreen than in the pages of a book, which is a commendable feat in its own right.
4 The Life of Chuck (2024)

Another Flanagan adaptation that outshines King’s book, The Life of Chuck makes great use of a competent foundation to add more layers to the tale of Charles "Chuck" Krantz (Tom Hiddleston). King’s novella follows a reverse-chronological structure that is tricky to adapt on screen, but Flanagan accomplishes this with ease. Competent character writing is one of Flanagan’s greatest strengths as a storyteller, along with his understanding of the human condition, which also includes grief. These qualities make Life of Chuck an atypical film, as it successfully translates some of the best moments from the book into unforgettable spectacle.
5 The Long Walk (2025)

Francis Lawrence’s The Long Walk is easily one of the best Stephen King adaptations in years. The film grounds the novel’s dystopian premise with expanded world-building, adding more impetus to the walk in question and why it’s important. As in the source material, the relationship between the characters is paramount, but Lawrence hones in on Ray Garraty (Cooper Hoffman) and Peter McVries (David Jonsson) to flesh out a more tactile bond. This emotional aspect radically improves an already solid source material, while an altered ending adds much-needed punch to a rather morose setting.
6 The Shawshank Redemption (1994)

The differences between The Shawshank Redemption and King’s Rita Hayworth and Shawshank Redemption are vast, as the Frank Darabont film takes a more dramatic approach suited in the cinematic medium. This not only yields a compelling movie, but also a wonderful adaptation, as Darabont takes the liberty of tweaking character arcs and shaping a more powerful ending. For example, Brooks Hatlen (James Whitmore) is a minor character in the book, but the film makes good use of his heartbreaking arc to highlight the psychological impact of prolonged institutionalization. There are also higher stakes peppered throughout, combined with Red’s (Morgan Freeman) unforgettable narration that makes the world feel more visceral and lived-in.
7 The Dead Zone (1983)

It’s tough to argue in favor of a better adaptation when it comes to The Dead Zone, a brilliant book that features some of the richest character studies from King. That said, David Cronenberg’s film is an anomaly of sorts, as it effectively sharpens narrative focus without sacrificing the heartbreaking highlights of the novel. Although the novel has more room to examine the banality of evil, Cronenberg trims subplots to pace this engaging story like a tense thriller. This version of Johnny Smith (Christopher Walken) also feels more isolated and haunted, opting for a quieter (and more relatable) sense of exhaustion due to his unpredictable psychic powers.
8 The Shining (1980)

“I think ‘The Shining’ is a beautiful film and it looks terrific, and as I’ve said before, it’s like a big, beautiful Cadillac with no engine inside it.” This is what King had to say about Kubrick’s celebrated adaptation, which is (rightfully) lauded as one of the best horror movies ever made. This is a rather complex situation, as King’s novel does offer a more nuanced examination of its characters, and is backed by greater emotional weight defining Jack and Wendy Torrance.

That said, Kubrick’s version is a cinematic masterpiece that turns the Overlook Hotel’s atmospheric terror into iconic pop culture imagery. The narrative is tight and unrelenting, painting an unnerving picture of Jack’s descent into madness, which is cushioned by unforgettable performances by Jack Nicholson and Shelley Duvall. Although “better” will always be subjective, Kubrick’s film is deliberately (and quite literally) colder, ending on an ambiguous note that still fuels endless theories and debates.
9 Carrie (1976)

Carrie was King’s first published book. It has influenced several adaptations, including Flanagan’s eight-episode series that hews closer to the source material (while taking some hefty liberties). Brian De Palma’s 1976 film, however, has colored our perception of Carrie White and what she stands for, even if that interpretation wildly diverges from the one in King’s novel. Even so, De Palma doesn’t opt for the novel’s epistolary structure to tell the story, as a more clean-cut and linear narrative makes for a sharper film. De Palma’s love for stylistic flair adds an edge to the prom sequence at the end, but the film succeeds in conveying the agonizing cruelty of growing up with thoughtless bullies.
10 Misery (1990)

Rob Reiner’s Misery is a more effective thriller than the one woven in the book, thanks to Kathy Bates’ Oscar-winning performance as Annie Wilkes, who brings a chilling magnetism to the character onscreen. Reiner also cut down on several asides and side-stories to keep the focus streamlined, which bodes well for a thriller that relies on escalating tension (and violence) to scare audiences. What remains is a heart-thumping cat-and-mouse game that brings some of the most iconic book moments to life. There’s also a sense of grim humor that blends well with the suffocating tension, making Misery a more balanced tale about obsessive fandom and creative control.

articles.headline: DistroKid has been quietly taking down songs in response to UMG lawsuit
keyFacts: DistroKid confirmed that it removed a small number of songs following a copyright lawsuit filed by UMG in September.
Artists reported that their non-AI tracks were removed without prior notice or adequate communication from DistroKid.
DistroKid's VP of Artist Services stated that the company disputes UMG's allegations and is working to minimize disruption for affected artists.
body: Artists are taking to social media to complain that DistroKid has unceremoniously removed their work without notice. Now DistroKid has confirmed to The Verge that the takedowns are a direct response to claims made by UMG. The label filed a lawsuit in September claiming that DistroKid has created an “AI-slop pipeline.” Artists are saying that their non-AI works are being caught up in the purge, however.
DistroKid has been quietly taking down songs in response to UMG lawsuit
Artists are frustrated with the lack of transparency around DistroKid removing their songs.

Musician and self-described “Video Game boy” McGwire reported that six of his songs had been removed from streaming. As has been the case with others, McGwire says that there was no communication from DistroKid before or after the removals, and that he had to contact the company for an explanation.

DistroKid also makes it exceedingly difficult to contact them. McGwire first had to have a “lengthy circular conversation” with a bot before getting hold of a live agent. One of the songs removed was a cover of Stevie Wonder’s “Isn’t She Lovely,” which he claims to have had a proper license for. Another track used a beat he purchased through a marketplace, which others had also licensed.
Most infuriating for McGwire was a song removed for an uncleared sample. The song he allegedly sampled was released two years after his track.

Much of the frustration from artists stems from the lack of communication and recourse. Nerdcore rapper Insane Ian posted that he “had an original song taken down with no warning, and they wouldn’t tell me why either.”

Rapper King Chase also struggled to get through to a person at DistroKid. He told The Verge that an entire album for an artist he had been working with was removed with no communication or explanation. “The album had been up for 3-4 years without incident,” he said, and that there had been “no copyright strikes or anything either.”

Amanda Ferri, DistroKid’s VP of Artist Services, told The Verge that “A very small number of recordings distributed through DistroKid have been removed in response to claims made by UMG. We strongly dispute the allegations underlying UMG’s lawsuit and regret the disruption to affected artists. We are working to minimize that disruption while protecting artists’ ability to release their music.”

articles.headline: Solanke strikes late as 10-man Spurs salvage point at Manchester United
keyFacts: Bryan Mbeumo scored for Manchester United in the 72nd minute before Rodrigo Bentancur was sent off for Tottenham following a challenge on Luke Shaw.
Dominic Solanke scored a header in added time to give 10-man Tottenham a 1-1 draw against Manchester United.
Tottenham remains winless in the relegation zone after six league games, while Manchester United sits in 12th place.
body: After 72 laboured minutes, this match was lit up by a moment of quality. Matheus Cunha was fed by Luke Shaw down the left and the Brazilian crossed to Bryan Mbeumo, who spun and finished for Manchester United.
It drew delirious chants of “you’re going down with the City” with Spurs, at that stage, rock bottom of the Premier League and Manchester City’s long-term future in the division in question.

Uglier scenes followed for Spurs when Shaw chased Bruno Fernandes ball, leading Rodrigo Bentancur to launch an ugly scissor challenge that, if it had connected with the left-back, might have caused serious injury.

An incensed Shaw, surely reminded of his horrific double-leg break sustained 11 years ago at PSV, hared after Bentancur and shoved him over. Up came the midfielder to push his head into Shaw’s, who went down as a melee ensued.
Stuart Attwell sent Bentancur off and the referee issued yellow cards to Shaw – lucky to escape a red, too, for the push – and Jan Paul van Hecke.
All of this followed what had been a near snoozefest in which Spurs could not finish and United were disjointed: the tale, in microcosm, of their seasons.

There was more, though, as Tottenham registered an added-time equaliser and only their third league goal this season. Senne Lammens and Lisandro Martínez were United’s culprits as Sandro Tonali’s floated cross from the left should have been cleared by the Argentine but, instead, Dominic Solanke out-fought him and headed past Lammens, who watched it go in.

While averting a fourth defeat, Spurs still remain winless after their opening six league games for only a fourth time. This draw means there is no clear answer to the pre-game question of which manager is under more pressure, as both Roberto De Zerbi and Michael Carrick remain in need of a victory.
When the Italian scans the table, he will see his beleaguered side off the bottom but still in the relegation zone, while Carrick’s United remain in 12th and with a solitary victory.
De Zerbi now takes his squad to Marbella for warm-weather training, while Carrick’s men are at Atlético Madrid on Tuesday in the Champions League. They both need to conjure something.

After volleys of “you cheating bastards, you know what you are” rang out from both sets of fans, Lammens struggled with a nightmare start. A loose pass was intercepted by Lucas Bergvall and the ball rolled into Solanke. Yet, as has been Spurs’ problem, the centre-forward failed to finish, his shot saved by a relieved Lammens, who was jittery again when Martínez passed to him on his goalline, where he dawdled before hoofing clear.

The reports had stated how De Zerbi’s men have played well, at times this season, but cannot finish: a hindrance in this sport. No boon, too, for any team is hesitation, as when Youri Tielemans waited for the ball to bounce, Tottenham pounced, and suddenly Sávio was heading forward, the sliding challenge of Leny Yoro, fielded today at right back, saving a scattered rearguard.

This pointed to a Spurs ascendancy that was a headscratcher for Carrick and yet more Spurs profligacy saved United when Mohammed Kudus’s cross found Archie Gray and the young right-back beat Lammens but not his right post.

Carrick wants his team to control contests but there was close to zero control throughout. On the hour Carlos Baleba entered for his debut and immediately spun and flicked deftly into Fernandes’ path and you were reminded what skill can do.
Now came the breathless denouement – a point, at the close, feeling about fair.

articles.headline: This Android Auto problem is affecting calls on foldable phones
keyFacts: Foldable phone owners report being unable to place outgoing calls through Android Auto while their devices are closed, according to user posts.
Users and forum posts suggest that the AI assistant Gemini may be responsible for the calling bug affecting various foldable phone models.
Google and Motorola representatives are investigating the issue, but no official fixes or workarounds have been issued yet.
body: This Android Auto problem is affecting calls on foldable phones
It seems like Gemini is to blame.

Owners of foldable phones are reportedly running into issues when trying to place outgoing calls using Android Auto. Posts on Reddit, as well as Google and Motorola forums, describe various foldable phones losing their ability to make calls when they're closed, as first reported by Android Authority. And Gemini might play a role in the calling quandary.

Users say that when their phones are closed and they instruct them to call someone, the call doesn't connect. One poster on Reddit said they get a message to "flip open to continue." Incoming calls seem to come through just fine. Several of the posters report the issue only started after they began using Gemini.

While there's no confirmation yet on what may be causing the bug, both Google and Motorola appear to be investigating. Responses in forums show company representatives collecting information about the incidents.
Which foldable phones are affected?

So far, most of the posts mention the Motorola Razr Ultra (specifically the 60 and 70 models) with Android 16 installed. A post from April mentioned issues with a Samsung Galaxy Z Flip 7 and also noted that there were no calling issues until the poster started using Gemini. Android 16 started rolling out in June 2025 with updates like live notification updates, camera improvements and scam detection features.

In that same Reddit post from about three months ago, one user said they had to switch back from Gemini to Google Assistant. After doing so, they were once again able to place outgoing calls while the foldable was closed. While that might seem like an easy enough fix, as of last month, Google pulled Google Assistant from phones, tablets and other devices. The transition began September 4, 2026 but only for phones that have the minimum requirements to run the AI service.
Is there a workaround?

Google and Motorola haven't issued any official fixes yet, and although foldable phone owners have detailed the lengths they've gone to in order to solve the problem, there doesn't seem to be a solution yet aside from making calls with the phones open.

The increased presence of Gemini across the Google ecosystem mirrors the broader push to integrate AI tools into everyday life. While some embrace the myriad AI tools popping up at every turn, others are less convinced, particularly in these early days when bugs may run amok. For some, like a few in these forum threads, the answer is turning to apps and products that don't use AI — or at least offer a way to turn it off.
